posts.cooked:
So, my friend and I tried playing Vengeance with the new multi-villain method finally, and got kicked to the curb. Friction was the first villain in the play order and ended up destroying us by locking down our player decks (via repeatedly destroying all of our ongoing and equipment cards). We focused and destroyed her, but not until all heroes were down into low single digit HP. We flipped Friction's card over only to be terribly dismayed that her incapacitate power was to keep destroying an ongoing or equipment card each time her turn came up. I felt particularly picked on, as I was playing Wraith (as did my friend with the Naturalist deck).

What's the secret to keeping player decks active with Friction playing in the game? I'm fine with a good challenge and all, but Friction made the game "unfun" by preventing the players from being able to build up their powers and then continuing to strip them. By the time she was killed, we couldn't get more than one ongoing or equipment card into play per hero, and then we had to decide which hero got the big "reset" when her turn came around. It was downright frustrating.

Any recommendations on how to play against her?

posts.name: mlangsdorf
posts.cooked:
Friction is tough, especially in a two player game, but it's perfectly feasible to build up against her. Naturalist has Natural Born Vigor, that lets him use two powers in a turn. With that out, it's perfectly viable to burn Naturalist's current form to satisfy Friction on her turn, play a new ongoing on your turn, use Naturalist's inherent power to recover the Form card, and then use whatever additional power you got from the Form or the new ongoing card. It's not ideal, and it's annoying, but it's not impossible.

I don't really recommend taking out Friction's dampeners with targeted damage. That's 9 damage that could be spent reducing her HP by 9, and there's no guarantee that she'll do 9 or more damage to herself from her own cards. (Obviously, if you have someone like Tempest doing a lot of lightning damage, that can change the calculus.) Her Stolen Gear is nasty, since it plays more cards and puts more Surges in her trash, making the cards she plays worse, so that's a reasonable target.

Locking down her deck can be worthwhile. Wraith and Naturalist can't lock her down completely, but Wraith can use IR Eyepiece to get rid of the cards that destroy ongoings. She's only got two Blinding Surges (which only destroy ongoings, so Wraith should be have nearly uneffected) so if you can control her ability to play multiple cards, you shouldn't have to worry about them until the end of the game.

posts.cooked:
Humble-Knight:

My experience is the opposite. Focus fire on one or two while plinking away at the others.

As a general rule–by which I mean it hasn’t always worked–I’ve preferred to have villains active just because there are ways to neutralize active villains. You can Ground Pound or Adhesive Foam or whatever to mitigate what they can do to you. Once they’re Incapacitated, though, those tricks don’t work and they just have a steady, unblockable stream of screw you. I agree that focusing on those whose Incapacitated effects aren’t so bad is perfectly okay, but generally speaking, I’d rather kill 'em all at once.

posts.name: Sefirit
posts.cooked:
I agree with the focus fire method.  The incap sides are much less dangerous than an active villain, especially if they have minions out.  It went against every fiber of my being but my group adopted a strategy of just focus fire each villain, not anything from their deck, just the actual villain one at a time.  After the first one or two (depending on H) go down the game gets much more managable.

This is the same reason we also ignore shock dampeners, just kill the villain as soon as possible so they stop drawing cards.  The idea of letting friction kill herself is nice, but we have found its better to just put that damage into her.  At 9 hit points, thats like what, more than a third of her overall life.  You can be well on your way to getting rid of her.

Overall I don't like the vengence format as much simply because we now have this strategy of pick a villain and completely ignore everything else on the table till its dead.  This strategy has been very effective.  In the 1-villain style games my group really tends to ignore the villain and deal with all the minions/ongoings/etc first which I enjoy more.
